title: Flatification of a projective generic curve and its horizontal marking
statement: Let $S$ be an excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring] integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] scheme with generic point [def-sc-generic-point] $\eta$. Let $h:C\to S$ be projective in the finite-projective-space sense [def-kun-projective], with $C$ integral and $C_\eta$ a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] irreducible curve of dimension $1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $H\subset C$ be the schematic closure of a finite etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] closed subscheme $H_\eta\subset C_\eta$ (possibly empty). There is an excellent integral Noetherian scheme $S_1$ and a projective-bundle birational morphism $v:S_1\to S$, which is a blowup with centre disjoint from a dense open of $S$, with the following properties. The schematic closures $C_1$ and $H_1$ of $C_\eta\times_S S_1$ and $H_\eta\times_S S_1$ in $C\times_S S_1$ are the strict transforms. The scheme $C_1$ is integral, $H_1\subset C_1$ is closed, $C_1\to S_1$ is projective in the finite-projective-space sense, flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] with every geometric fibre of pure dimension $1$, and $H_1\to S_1$ is finite, flat and finitely presented with all nonempty geometric fibres of pure dimension $0$. These transforms have their original generic fibres, and the projection $C_1\to C$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and birational. A blowup in an ideal sheaf $I$ is the relative Proj of $\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n$; schematic closure is defined by the kernel of restriction of functions to the given subscheme.

Stacks Tag 081R (flat-lemma-flat-after-blowing-up), applied to their disjoint union; Tag 0GSJ (more-morphisms-lemma-flat-associated-equidimensional), with F=O on each horizontal integral component, gives the pure relative dimensions. Excellence: Tag 07QU (more-algebra-lemma-finite-type-over-excellent).

proof.text: By [lem-pc-projective-proper], $C\to S$ is proper; its closed marking $H\to S$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Apply [lem-trf-simultaneous-proper-generic-flattening] to these two proper families. It gives a common nonempty open $U$, one admissible blowup $v:S_1\to S$, and strict transforms $\widetilde C,\widetilde H$ flat and finitely presented over $S_1$, agreeing with the original families away from the centre. Empty $H$ is allowed.

source.place: Tag 081R, lemma-flat-after-blowing-up, applied to a finite disjoint union after Morphisms Tag 052A, proposition-generic-flatness; Divisors Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform. ILO Expose X, Theorem 3.4 proof Step 2, printed p.160.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-excellent-blowup-projective-transforms] to this blowup: its ideal is finite type and unit on the nonempty $U$. Thus $S_1$ is excellent, integral and Noetherian, and $v$ is proper, birational and projective in the projective-bundle sense. Since $C\to S$ has a finite-projective-space embedding and $\widetilde C$ is closed in its base change, the same lemma gives finite-projective-space projectivity of $\widetilde C\to S_1$.

source.place: Tag 0804, lemma-blowing-up-affine; Tag 02NS, lemma-blowing-up-projective (Sym-to-Rees closed immersion); More on Algebra Tag 07QU, lemma-finite-type-over-excellent. Retained proof Steps 3--4 of the parent, including the two distinct projectivity conventions.

proof.text: The generic curve is nonempty, so the integral $C$ dominates $S$. The transforms from Step 1 are the closures over the centre complement, a nonempty open where $v$ is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-trf-flat-strict-transform-generic-closures] with that open: flatness of both transforms is from Step 1; properness of $v$, its isomorphism over the centre complement, and integrality and Noetherianity of $S_1$ are from Step 2. This identifies $\widetilde C=C_1$ and $\widetilde H=H_1$ with the stated generic closures, proves $C_1$ integral and $H_1\subset C_1$ closed, retains both generic fibres and proves $C_1\to C$ proper birational.

source.place: Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform, schematic-closure description; ILO Expose X Theorem 3.4, paragraph before the proof and Step 2, printed p.160. Flat generic-density and integrality argument supplied in retained parent proof Steps 5--6.

proof.text: Finite-projective-space projectivity makes $C_1\to S_1$ proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper]. Apply [lem-trf-flat-proper-curve-marking-fibres] to $C_1,H_1$: Step 1 supplies flat finite presentation, Step 3 generic density and the generic identifications, and the hypotheses give the irreducible dimension-one generic curve and finite etale generic marking. The curve has nonempty pure dimension-one geometric fibres and the marking is finite flat finitely presented with pure dimension-zero nonempty geometric fibres. Steps 1--3 provide all remaining assertions.

lean.note: Uses the canonical admissible blowup and strict-transform APIs. Closed immersions and equality of their kernel ideal sheaves specify the closures and strict transforms up to their unique isomorphisms over the ambient schemes. Generic-fibre pullback squares include their embedding compatibility. Finite presentation is locally finite presentation together with the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness supplied by H-projectivity or finiteness.
